clue.text: Goddess of Irish media novelist's written about

indicators.note: the novelist's name is set down around the broadcaster's initials, enclosing them

parts.note: Martin or Kingsley Amis, the British novelists
RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster, Raidió Teilifís Éireann

explanation.surface: A goddess is the subject of a novelist's piece in the Irish press.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis is the Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon, so a direct example of a goddess.

clue.text: A mother? He never had one!

definitions.text: A mother? He never had one!

parts.words: A mother? He never had one!
parts.note: the first man in Genesis was made from dust, so he had no mother

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a mother and is told the man in question never had one.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid's ADAK is a slip: the clue plainly points to the first man in Genesis, and this letter is unchecked.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the first man was formed directly by God, so he alone had no mother.

clue.text: Credit for a parasite?

definitions.meaning: buying on ... means buying on credit, in British slang
a small bloodsucking arachnid that clings to animals

explanation.definitionFit: Tick is British slang for credit, and also the name of a bloodsucking mite-like parasite.

clue.text: Route with a string of annoyances?

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written here as MI
a string of things is a series

explanation.surface: A road comes with a long run of irritations.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a London-to-Leeds motorway; crosswords read its 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Miseries are sources of distress, so troubles or annoyances in a loose sense.

clue.text: Season without nature's first shoot

indicators.note: the season is written without the letter that follows

parts.note: spring is one of the four seasons

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word nature

explanation.surface: A season lacking natural growth still produces a shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: SPRING without N (first of 'nature's') gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small shoot or twig of a plant.

clue.text: One seems poorly, vomiting

indicators.note: feeling poorly suggests things are out of order, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone looks unwell and is being sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Emesis is the medical term for being sick, so a technical synonym for vomiting.

clue.text: Grieve over English and Irish mountains

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first word is placed over the second

parts.note: to grieve is to mourn

explanation.surface: Someone laments the loss of English and Irish peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mournes are a granite range in County Down, Northern Ireland, so these are Irish mountains.

clue.text: Inviolable development one can't cross

indicators.note: development of the letters means working them into a new shape

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A building plan that nobody is allowed to cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges A (one) with CANT and CROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacrosanct is too sacred to be violated or interfered with.

clue.text: Short hose with short top for thickset build

annotationWithheld.why: Short hose with short top for thickset build: STOCKIN(G) fits 'Short hose', but no reading of 'short top' gives the remaining ESS, and no blog or database parse was found
annotationWithheld.clue: Short hose with short top for thickset build

clue.text: Any entitled to carry a form of crest may be proud of it

definitions.text: Any entitled to carry a form of crest may be proud of it

indicators.note: one word bears another inside it, as a bag carries its load
a form of a word is a reshaping of its letters

explanation.surface: Anyone with the right to bear a family crest may take pride in their lineage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a form of' turns the crest into CESTR and 'to carry' signals the enclosure. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a right to bear a family crest comes from one's lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is what entitles a family to its coat of arms, and it is what such people take pride in.

clue.text: Messenger with a sister about 10

parts.note: a sister in a religious order is a nun
C stands for circa, Latin for about
the figures 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A courier travels with a nun, roughly ten of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 10 as the letters IO is a visual trick, not a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is a papal envoy, an ambassador who carries the Pope's messages to a government.

clue.text: A good man is ready for first promotion

parts.note: ST, for saint, is crossword shorthand for a good man
ripe means ready, as fruit is

explanation.surface: A virtuous man is ready to rise for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier's first step up the ranks earns a stripe on the sleeve, so it stands for promotion.

clue.text: Badger about one of 22 with 15, which is novel

indicators.note: the badger's name goes around the shortened title

parts.note: Brock is a traditional name for the badger

indicators.note: entry 15 is the dropping of an opening sound, so the first letter of the second word is lost

parts.note: members of the Privy Council are styled Right Honourable, abbreviated Right Hon

explanation.surface: A badger surrounds a privy councillor in a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with 15' applies aphaeresis (losing an initial sound) to HON, giving ON; RIGHT ON then sits inside BROCK ('about').
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene's 1938 crime story set on the south coast is a famous example of a novel.

clue.text: Rewritable record

parts.note: suggests a modern disc or tape, but means an ancient manuscript scraped and written over

explanation.surface: Looks like a description of a recordable disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A palimpsest is a parchment whose original text was scraped off so it could be written on again.

clue.text: Booster of retail trade?

parts.note: a booster seems to promote shops, but in slang a booster is a thief who steals from them

explanation.surface: Looks like praise for someone who helps the high street.
explanation.definitionFit: Booster is American slang for a store thief, so this person takes goods from shops without paying.

clue.text: Herbert sees air trip, which takes off first

parts.note: A. P. Herbert, the humorist and MP, signed his pieces A.P.H.

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer watches an airborne excursion that departs first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges the letters, making AERESIS. The definition is self-describing: the word names the dropping of a word's opening sound, which is exactly what it says.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphaeresis is the loss of a word's initial sound, as in 'bus' from omnibus: something taken off the front.

clue.text: Use space to manoeuvre

parts.note: an em is a printer's space, the width of an M
a ploy is a cunning manoeuvre

explanation.surface: Make use of room in which to manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ something is to put it to use.

clue.text: A beard makes a woman lose heart

indicators.note: a word that loses its heart keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Growing facial hair causes a woman to become discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: WOMAN without its middle gives WN, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is the bristly growth on barley or grass ears, which botanists call its beard.

clue.text: Hooked one; caught, extra cover

indicators.note: the outer word covers the letters placed inside it

parts.note: extra means added
one is the Roman numeral I
Ct is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught or catches

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a batsman hooks, and is caught at extra cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all cricket: a hook is a batting stroke and extra cover a fielding position, so 'cover' hides its job of enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hooked on something means being dependent on it, the state of an addict.

clue.text: The devil lies in oversimplification

indicators.note: the run of letters lies inside the longer word

explanation.surface: Oversimplifying is where the trouble lies.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'the devil is in the detail'.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a small mischievous demon, so a little devil.

clue.text: Gaming equipment occurs with 15 about supplements

indicators.note: the shortened verb goes around the gaming pieces
entry 15 is the loss of an opening sound, so the first letter goes

parts.note: occurs means happens
dice are used in games of chance

explanation.surface: Gambling gear shows up alongside a word about extra material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with 15' cuts H from HAPPENS to give APPENS, which goes 'about' DICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Appendices are sections added at the end of a book, so supplements to the main text.

clue.text: Where first cough syrup was concocted?

definitions.text: Where first cough syrup was concocted?

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word cough
the letters of syrup are mixed up to make something new

explanation.surface: A question about the birthplace of the first cough mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was concocted' mixes the letters into YPRUS. The whole clue is the definition, a whimsical question answered by a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue asks for a place, and this Mediterranean island is a country, so a fitting answer to where.

clue.text: Municipal convenience switched round to make it PC

indicators.note: the two words are taken in the reverse of the order the clue gives

parts.note: a privy is a toilet, which British English politely calls a convenience
a municipal body is a council

explanation.surface: A town's public toilet is turned around to make it politically correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switched round' reverses the order of the two words. The surface teases with PC's other senses, politically correct and police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: PC is the standard abbreviation for the Privy Council, the body of advisers to the British sovereign.

clue.text: Island where old colonist reversed poles

indicators.note: the north and south poles swap places, so the letters standing for them change ends

parts.note: the Saxons settled England in the fifth and sixth centuries

explanation.surface: An island where an ancient settler turned the poles around.
explanation.walkthrough: SAXON begins with S and ends with N, the poles; swapping them gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Naxos is the largest island of the Cyclades in the Aegean Sea.

clue.text: Legal document could be holy

definitions.meaning: a court order such as a summons
the phrase holy ..., meaning sacred scripture

explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal court order, and holy writ is a name for scripture.

clue.text: It's frozen, only a tenth showing up

indicators.note: in a down entry, showing up means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: deci- is the prefix meaning one tenth

explanation.surface: Only a tenth of something frozen shows above the water, as with an iceberg.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iced has been chilled until frozen, like a frozen lake.

clue.text: To demand with violence used to be wrong

parts.note: ex means former, what something used to be
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Making violent demands was once considered wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To extort is to obtain something by force or threats, a demand backed by violence.

clue.text: The Queen in outlandish dress fit to be seen in public

definitions.text: fit to be seen in public

indicators.note: the royal letters go inside the strange garb

parts.note: outlandish clothing is exotic
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Her Majesty in bizarre clothing is fit for public view.
explanation.definitionFit: Exoteric teaching is meant for outsiders, the general public, as opposed to esoteric doctrine for initiates.

clue.text: Hospital trust without significant push

indicators.note: in the old sense, without means outside, so the trust surrounds the letter

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: An NHS hospital trust lacks any real drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrust is a strong forceful shove, and the thrust of an argument is its main drive.

clue.text: Thus one could appear in deadest condition

definitions.text: Thus one could appear in deadest condition

indicators.note: the letters are put into a different condition, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: This is how someone in a lifeless state might look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condition' rearranges DEADEST. The whole clue also defines: a heavily drugged patient looks dead to the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient given calming drugs lies limp and motionless, looking almost lifeless.
